body: Forward test of the sector cycle/lead indicator method (NOT a recommendation; not buy/sell). Probability 0.60 (naive base rate 0.55) that: PNC Financial Q4 2026 net interest income is ≥$4,250 m. Evidence: Q3 2026 financial highlights (Oct-2026): NII $4,206m (+2% QoQ, +15% YoY incl. FirstBank), NIM 2.94%; Q2 2026 NII $4,107m, Q3 2025 $3,648m; 'commercial loan growth and higher yields on interest-earning assets, partially offset by increased funding costs'; efficiency ratio 57%; Q4 buybacks to approximate Q3. US 10-yr yield Q4-to-date average 5.07% vs 4.75% in Q3 (Yahoo ^TNX). Reasoning: Lead indicator: higher long rates keep lifting yields on PNC's repricing fixed-rate securities and loans (a multi-year tailwind the bank has cited), while loan growth continues; funding costs are the offset. $4,250m is only +1% QoQ, below the recent QoQ pace, so we lean slightly above the base. Resolution: YES if PNC's reported total net interest income (GAAP, not fully taxable-equivalent) for the quarter ended 31-Dec-2026 is ≥$4,250m per its Q4 2026 earnings release. Source: PNC Q4 2026 financial highlights / earnings release (8-K, EDGAR). Resolve by 2027-01-31; score with Brier vs base rate.

data.base_rate_reasoning: Naive: NII rose QoQ in each of the last two reported quarters; a ≥1% QoQ rise in the next quarter has roughly 55% odds for a large regional bank.
